eng_blog.notes: The blog index and technical deep dives document how Fly builds tokens and clusters; both deep dives are by Thomas Ptacek, identified as a Fly.io software engineer.

claygent-argon-B.reasoning: I used Fly.io’s own About page for the 2017 founding-year statement and its company LinkedIn page for Chicago headquarters, noting third-party source conflicts where relevant. The official July 24, 2026 announcement documents both the $25 million Series D and Scott Johnston joining as CEO, within the requested windows. The November 9 changelog lists a newly available Sprites wallet/payment feature. The careers index lists four openings and none is an AI/ML or SDR/BDR/AE role. The remaining fields follow the cited first-party product, blog, documentation, compliance, customer, pricing and vendor pages.

hq_location.notes: Fly.io’s LinkedIn company profile and Craft location listing give Chicago; some financial-data profiles report San Francisco, so this follows the company profile.

public_docs.notes: The public developer documentation has guides and reference material for Fly Machines, Sprites, Managed Postgres, networking and flyctl.

raised_18mo.notes: The July 2026 Series D announcement is within the 18 months before November 9, 2026.

founded_year.notes: Fly.io says it has been building its public cloud since 2017; some third-party profiles report 2016, so I follow the company’s own account.

last_funding.notes: Fly.io announced the $25 million Series D on July 24, 2026.

launched_6mo.notes: The November 9, 2026 changelog announces “Pocket money for agents,” a new Sprites feature connecting Stripe Link for agent-approved one-time purchases.

pricing_page.notes: The public page lists pricing for Fly Machines, Sprites, Managed Postgres and other services.

employee_band.notes: PitchBook lists 58 employees and LinkedIn reports 56; both fall in the 51-100 band.

hiring_sdr_ae.notes: The current job index lists four openings and none is titled SDR, BDR, sales/business development representative, or account executive.

model_provider.notes: Fly.io documents OpenRouter as a model-access Connector using the customer’s key. Separately, its security questionnaire says Anthropic and OpenAI are used only for Fly.io internal tooling.
model_provider.value: OpenRouter (through an optional user-configured Connector for model access)

named_customers.notes: Fly.io says these agent-first companies use its platform to build production AI applications.

ai_ml_roles_open.notes: The current job index lists four roles—Fullstack Engineer, Infrastructure Operations Engineer, Account Manager, and Networking Engineer—and none is an AI, ML or data-science role.

compliance_certs.notes: The security questionnaire names SOC 2 Type 2 and a HIPAA BAA; it says Fly.io does not hold ISO 27001 or a PCI DSS AOC.

crm_stack_signal.notes: The sub-processor list identifies HubSpot for customer relationship management and Customer.io for newsletters and transactional email.

product_one_liner.notes: The homepage describes its global cloud, Fly Machines and Sprites; the Sprites documentation identifies AI agents and code execution as use cases.
product_one_liner.value: Fly.io is a global public cloud for developers to run applications and databases near users, with hardware-isolated Linux computers for AI agents and code execution.

leadership_change_12mo.notes: The July 24, 2026 announcement says Scott Johnston joined as CEO and board member.
